races.name: Betway Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rogue Millions
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ideally suited to contested pace, 266 days off but classy handicap debut winner who handles good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Highly impressive C&D winner (soft ground; handles good) on handicap debut last June; didn't build on that in two subsequent runs but has been gelded and switched stables; still low-mileage and his new yard has been among the winners; fascinating contender.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Patient type who stays well, 266-day absence a concern but trainer has 2/33 recent record suggesting patience
runners_data.spotlight: A third runner for Ian Williams; ran some fine races in defeat last season, including at Glorious Goodwood (1m6f, good to soft); returns after nine months off over a trip probably short of his optimum.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up in trip after shaping well over 1m2f at York, each-way claims if stamina holds
runners_data.comment: Has failed to kick on since his good run over C&D last August but he's not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable sixth over 1m2f both starts this year, the latter in a warm race at York when shaping as if worth another try over 1m3f+; gets that here and has each-way hopes.

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from Dubai winter, 4lb higher than last British win and probably needs this run
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned in the UAE this winter, last seen finishing tailed off at Meydan; still 4lb higher than for his last win in Britain and probably best watched after three months off.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with excellent recent form, 7lb claimer Lauren Young takes valuable weight off
runners_data.comment: 1-14 on turf; second of six in this last year but a supporting role again seems likely
runners_data.spotlight: Tough 6yo with seven wins to his name; beaten favourite at Hamilton (1m3f, good) last time but shaped quite nicely, keeping on into second place after a slow start and meeting trouble; place possibilities again at the very least.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Hold-up type plagued by slow starts, needs to break cleanly to be competitive off this mark
runners_data.comment: Neck C&D 2nd last August and last month's Musselburgh run can be upgraded; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 2lb lower at Newcastle last autumn but hasn't repeated the form and slow starts are becoming a habit; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: Front-runner with William Buick aboard, good recent form and tactical speed to cope with Claymore's challenge
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins from 11 starts; successful on comeback at Kempton (1m4f, AW; made all) in April and again ran well when second at Newmarket (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; should be in the thick of things once more.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Front-running filly in excellent form, Saffie Osborne knows her well and she handles this trip perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Likeable front-running filly; made a winning return at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) and typically gave her all when second at Hamilton (1m5f, good) three weeks later; edging up the weights but set for another bold show.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Irish hold-up horse on long losing run, veteran with limited potential for improvement
runners_data.comment: Regressing but handicapper relenting and ground more to suit now
runners_data.spotlight: Irish-trained 8yo, on a long losing sequence; not entirely disgraced when fourth of ten at Leopardstown (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; others have more potential but he's certainly well treated on his best form.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying top weight, poor recent British form makes him hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Hasn't won since 2023 and faces a stiff task on these terms
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth in handicap in Saudi Arabia on second start this year but has not beaten a rival in two runs back in Britain; difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran returning to turf after AW success, 9-year-old faces unexposed younger rivals
runners_data.spotlight: Durable veteran who won twice on the AW early this year; however, he was soundly beaten at Newcastle on Good Friday and faces some unexposed rivals on his return to turf.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose Listed third at Hamilton looks a fluke performance, hard to trust this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Close third of seven in Listed event at Hamilton (1m3f, good; 150-1) last summer, but that run stands out like a sore thumb from the rest of his form and he was well beaten (after wind surgery) over the same C&D on reappearance; too much to prove for comfort.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 11-month break, classy form when fresh and Haggas/Doyle combination respected
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; good fourth in Listed race at Goodwood last spring; gelded and off 11 months, shaped promisingly when third of 14 on handicap debut at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago, doing his best work late on; nudged up 1lb but still looks seriously unexposed; strong claims.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore and Topteam will dispute the early lead, with Ghaiyya likely prominent just behind this pair. The dual pace angle creates an honest gallop over this stamina-testing 1m3f trip, with the leaders unable to steal cheap sectionals. Behind them, the large contingent of hold-up horses including Rogue Millions, Dancing In Paris, Castle Stuart and Opportunity will be looking for the race to develop into their hands. This race shape strongly favours the closers and hold-up merchants, as the contested pace will set up a proper test of stamina where late-running types can pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore and Topteam go too hard early and weaken dramatically
scenarios.body: The honest gallop becomes a slog, perfectly suiting the patient hold-up horses who can unleash their finishing kicks. Late runners get the perfect setup as the pace setters capitulate in the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays strong but manageable throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a proper stamina test where class and ability prevail over tactics. Horses with the best form and ratings can utilize the fair pace to show their true merit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Compromise
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders ease up mid-race creating stop-start fractions
scenarios.body: The race loses its rhythm and becomes more tactical than a pure stamina test. Prominent racers and those with tactical speed can capitalize on the uneven tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly moderate allowing many to stay in contention
scenarios.body: The large field stays bunched turning for home creating a cavalry charge finish. Horses with the best turn of foot rather than pure stamina gain the advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch Claymore's jumping from the gates as slow starts have become habitual and he needs to lead to be effective
Monitor the pace through the first half-mile as both Claymore and Topteam will want to dictate terms early
Observe how quickly the hold-up horses can get into contention turning for home with so many needing room late
Keep an eye on the ground conditions as several runners including Rogue Millions have specific going preferences
Watch for market moves on the 266-day absentees Rogue Millions and Dancing In Paris as stable confidence indicators

races.name: Betway Reverence Handicap

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but warning signs of fading in finish, 10-year-old veteran needs everything to fall right
runners_data.spotlight: Spent last year in the grip of the handicapper after seven wins in 2024; more leniently treated now and ran respectably when sixth of 28 in the 7f Victoria Cup at Ascot; seemed unsuited by drop back to 5f next time; this intermediate trip is probably ideal these days and he commands respect.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but form has tailed off this year, needs to turn corner from disappointing recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Had a solid 2025, winning three times (5f/6f), but hasn't finished in the first eight this year; dropping in the weights but needs to turn a corner; perhaps a change of headgear will help.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse coming into form with back-to-back wins, headgear on suggests connections expect more improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back 6f wins at Windsor (good to firm) and Ascot (good to soft) in 2025; has taken a while to get going this season but he shaped as if coming to the boil when sixth of 14 at Newbury (led briefly over 1f out) two weeks ago; back to his last winning mark and should be at concert pitch now.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but still racing above last winning mark, recent York eighth was disappointing
runners_data.comment: All the sharper for reappearance when second at Thirsk (6f) three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: His six successes include four last season; retains all his ability but he's still above his last winning mark and he was only eighth at York last Saturday.

runners_data.name: Station X
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who should get uncontested lead, career best at Southwell suggests ability is there
runners_data.comment: 2lb rise puts him on a career-high mark into a more competitive handicap, down from 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who posted a career best when seeing off five rivals at Southwell (6f) in April; beaten only narrowly when sixth in blanket finish at Hamilton (5f, good) last time; reliable, and should be in the mix again.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but poor turf record (1-27), headgear on but others more convincing
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner, only 1-27 on grass; never the slightest threat on return to turf at Leicester; others have more convincing profiles.

runners_data.name: Recency Bias
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with progressive profile, 5lb claimer reduces weight burden effectively
runners_data.comment: Never travelled on handicap debut but he impressed in his novice here the run before
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo with a progressive profile; beaten neck when odds-on at Newcastle (7f) last month; usually travels strongly and should be at least as effective back at 6f; still on a workable mark and high on the list.

runners_data.name: Marty Hopkirk
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed encouragement at Windsor, better suited to this distance
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo but he's been up and down so far
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced in last four handicaps but there was more encouragement in his fourth to Redorange (runs in the Listed race at 2.33) at Windsor 12 days ago; has raced mainly at 5f but should stay further; not without hope.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with all-or-nothing profile, 45 days off may need this run after Haydock win
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo with something of an all-or-nothing profile; put everything together when bolting up at Haydock (6f, good to soft) last autumn; might have needed the run when only ninth of 13 at Newmarket on reappearance; leading claims if building on that and cheekpieces may give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form at seven, narrow Ripon defeat shows ability remains intact
runners_data.comment: Began this year with two Newcastle wins but was disappointing there latest; risks attached
runners_data.spotlight: Almost as good as ever at the age of seven and went down narrowly at Ripon (6f, good) earlier this month; hard to knock but this is a warm race and he faces some unexposed rivals.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who found only Realign too strong at Haydock, strong form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Found only Realign too strong at Haydock (6f, good to soft) last autumn despite meeting trouble at a crucial stage, and he was back on the up when a neck second of 16 at Ripon (6f, good to soft) six weeks ago; reliable and has notably solid credentials.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who met trouble at York, better than bare form suggests
runners_data.comment: Merely 5th on last two runs but won this last year and is on a competitive mark if on song
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second on reappearance at Newcastle and better than the bare results suggest since, meeting significant trouble in running in a big field at York last time; could play a major role if getting the breaks.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse out of sorts since December win, needs revival but well handicapped on old form
runners_data.comment: Campaigned on AW for current stable; well handicapped on best turf form
runners_data.spotlight: Out of sorts since December AW success, finishing in midfield at York (40-1) on return to turf last time; beginning to look well handicapped but needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse racing 6lb above last winning mark, more exposed than main rivals
runners_data.comment: String of solid efforts for Ethan Tindall in the past nine months; has to be considered
runners_data.spotlight: Went close at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) on reappearance but had no obvious excuses at Doncaster next time; more exposed than some of these and 6lb above his highest winning mark.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent Ayr success over 7f, lightly raced and distance drop could suit
runners_data.comment: Down the field elsewhere on his two starts this season but his sole win came over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have come over 7f at Ayr, and he surged back to form when scoring there ten days ago; still lightly raced, in excellent hands, and should be at least as effective over this trip on a stiff track; a danger to all at the foot of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Station X is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and should dictate terms uncontested through moderate fractions over this 6f trip. Jordan Electrics and Dark Cloud Rising will sit prominent but neither is aggressive enough to pressure the leader early. The lack of pace pressure will create a tactical race where the speed horses can sustain their effort longer, while hold-up horses face the challenge of making up ground in a potentially strung-out finish. This shape strongly favours front-running and prominent racers who can position close to Station X without expending energy in pace battles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Station X gets an easy lead without early pressure...
scenarios.body: Station X controls the tempo and kicks clear in the final furlong while prominent racers like Wild Clary and Marty Hopkirk chase home. The hold-up brigade gets insufficient pace to aim at and struggle to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Jordan Electrics or Dark Cloud Rising press Station X early...
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and creates opportunities for horses with tactical speed like Recency Bias and Brosay to strike late. Station X may weaken under pressure allowing the prominent horses to dominate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses completely and becomes crawling...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where closers like Realign and Grant Wood can use their turn of foot. Mister Sox and Fivethousandtoone could also benefit from the tactical nature despite their questionable form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady and the favourites underperform...
scenarios.body: Native Honey's recent Ayr win suggests improvement and the distance drop could suit, while Gressington's low weight becomes significant. Both represent value if the market leaders fail to fire.

watchPoints.text: Station X could get too easy a lead if no early pressure develops, making them very hard to peg back
Jordan Electrics has pattern of fading in finish which could be costly in competitive handicap
Realign's 45-day absence after inconsistent profile raises questions about readiness to fire
Native Honey dropping back to 6f after 7f Ayr win with Saffie Osborne taking over from claim rider
Wild Clary and Brosay both have headgear changes suggesting connections expect improved efforts

races.name: Betway Achilles Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Rogue Lightning
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from Qatar success but 20 days since last run could leave him short of peak fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Globetrotting gelding whose last win came in Qatar (6f, good) in February 2025 when Washington Heights was second; has run respectably on his two outings this season, fourth in French Group 3 (5f, soft) on latest; should be thereabouts under optimum conditions.

runners_data.name: Washington Heights
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose Listed-winning form at York gives him strong claims if he can track the early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Close third in Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock 12 months ago and made most to win Listed race at York (5f, good to firm) last summer; well below par all four starts since (short of room in Newmarket Group 3 on latest) but down in grade here and may well bounce back.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Class hold-up horse returning from 347-day layoff makes fitness a major concern despite Grade 1-winning ability
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class form when third in Group 1 Nunthorpe at York and when winning Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint at Del Mar, both in 2024; rusty on last year's reappearance but showed he retains plenty of ability when fourth of 20 in Group 1 King Charles III at Royal Ascot on only subsequent outing; leading claims if showing his best after layoff, although that's not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Celandine
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with sustainable style perfectly suited to controlling this small field from the front
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 since winning the Group 2 Lowther (6f, good to firm) as a 2yo, although she had an excuse (awkward leaving stalls, never a threat) in 6f Listed event at Newmarket (13-2) on reappearance; below par on two previous attempts at 5f, but not ruled out if on a going day for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Redorange
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist in peak form after Windsor success 12 days ago and wears tongue-tie for the first time
runners_data.comment: Didn't get much luck when an eye-catcher on York reappearance four days ago; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Classy sprinter who built on an eye-catching reappearance when justifying strong support in handicap at Windsor (5f, good) 12 days ago; found only one too good in French Listed event last summer and looks a strong contender back in this grade.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Late-swooping mare who won Listed race at Bath and wears tongue-tie and blinkers, 55 days off could be ideal
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo mare who sprang a 22-1 surprise in Listed race at Bath (5f, good) in April, swooping fast and late; likeable type with an impressive strike-rate but she'll need another personal best under a penalty.

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling since stable switch but Daniel Tudhope's 5lb claim brings him into calculations
runners_data.spotlight: 5-10 at 6f/7f for Harry Charlton; unplaced all four outings since joining current stable, finishing in midfield in Victoria Cup at Ascot most recently; unproven at 5f; wears headgear for the first time; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Luna A Inbhir Nis
runners_data.note: Front-running type likely to press Celandine early which could compromise both their chances late on
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who was a highly progressive 3yo last season, winning here; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; most progressive last season, making it six wins for the campaign in handicap at York (5.4f, good) in July;  probably needed the run when down the field there on reappearance; stiffer task up in grade.

races.paceDynamic: Celandine will lead this small field from the outset, with Washington Heights and Ten Pounds likely to track her in second and third positions early. The confirmed front-runner Celandine faces no obvious pace pressure, allowing her to dictate comfortable fractions through the first half of this 5f sprint. With most rivals (Rogue Lightning, Starlust, Redorange, Azure Angel) drawn to hold-up tactics, the race sets up as a tactical affair where the pace-setters can control proceedings before the closers launch their challenges in the final 2f. This sustained tempo strongly favors prominent runners who can position close to the pace without expending energy, as the hold-up brigade may find insufficient gallop to maximize their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Celandine sets uncontested fractions and Washington Heights tracks her smoothly
scenarios.body: The front two maintain their advantage as the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on the steady tempo. Prominent runners who saved energy early have enough left to resist the late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tell Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and the race turns into a 2f sprint finish
scenarios.body: Superior class horses Starlust and Redorange find the strong gallop they need to unleash devastating late kicks. The tactical nature allows them to overcome their hold-up styles with pure ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Celandine gets an easy lead and quickens clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The 4yo filly capitalizes on her uncontested position and sustainable pace to build an unassailable advantage. Her rivals are caught flat-footed by her sudden injection of pace when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Swoop Special
scenarios.trigger: If Azure Angel gets the perfect hold-up trip with strong pace throughout
scenarios.body: The Bath Listed winner repeats her 22-1 shock tactics with a perfectly timed late surge from the back. Her proven ability to produce explosive finishing speed catches the field napping.

watchPoints.text: Luna A Inbhir Nis may press Celandine for the early lead which would create a much stronger pace favoring hold-up horses
Starlust returning from 347-day absence makes her fitness levels impossible to assess despite her proven class edge
Redorange wears tongue-tie for first time which could unlock improvement from his Windsor handicap success
Washington Heights has disappointed in all four starts this season despite his previous Listed-winning form
Azure Angel's 22-1 Bath Listed success suggests she remains capable of big-priced surprises when the pace develops

races.name: Betway Lester Piggott Fillies' Stakes (Group 3) (Formerly Known As The Pinnacle Stakes)

runners_data.name: Estrange
runners_data.note: Defended this race successfully last year but faces a 224-day absence and needs to prove her wellbeing first time back
runners_data.spotlight: Very talented 5yo whose two wins last year included this race (1m4f, good; at Haydock) on reappearance; ran a cracker when second in Group 1 at Ascot (1m4f, good) on final start; that makes her the clear form pick back in this grade and she's the one to beat if ready to roll after 224 days off.

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Stablemate of the likely leader but prefers to come from behind, creating an ideal tactical setup for Owen Burrows
runners_data.spotlight: Stablemate of Azaniya; seemed to relish the step up to 1m6f when winning the Group 2 Lillie Langtry at Goodwood (good to soft) last summer; didn't give her running in Group 1 at Ascot on final 3yo start, finishing well behind Estrange; may still have untapped potential but this trip looks a bare minimum.

runners_data.name: Azaniya
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who will control the pace but faces stronger opposition than in recent Listed success
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed well last season, her four wins from just five outings culminating in a clearcut Listed success at Saint-Cloud (1m2f, heavy; also handles good to firm); shaped as if needing the run when fifth in Group 3 there on reappearance; gives the impression she'll relish this extra yardage, and with further improvement on the cards she's high on the list.

runners_data.name: Crepe Suzette
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose Group 2 Park Hill third represents the strongest form line in this field
runners_data.spotlight: Ended her 3yo campaign with an excellent third in Doncaster's Group 2 Park Hill Stakes (14.5f, good to soft); bit disappointing when only fifth in Listed race at Goodwood (11-8 favourite; beaten over 7l by Coedana) on return; now on a retrieval mission in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Coedana
runners_data.note: Improving hold-up horse whose Goodwood second came from an impossible position, suggesting untapped potential
runners_data.comment: Proved very progressive last season; steps up in grade but capable of further improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Improving with virtually every run, and was even better than the bare result when second in Listed race at Goodwood (1m4f, good; came from a long way back) four weeks ago; up in grade again but still has more in the tank and not to be underestimated.

runners_data.name: Sharpen
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner besides the leader but returns after 242 days under new connections
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win in Ireland came in 1m2f maiden but she was also a good second in a 1m4f Listed event; changed hands for 360,000gns in December; plenty of improvement required on British debut but she has switched to a flourishing stable and is not without hope.

runners_data.name: Patagonia Girl
runners_data.note: In-form handicapper stepping up significantly in class but recent Chester win shows current wellbeing
runners_data.comment: Went close over 1m2f on seasonal debut; unexposed over 1m4f but has an awkward draw
runners_data.spotlight: Has made incremental progress over 11 starts, overcoming a wide draw when beating 14 rivals in handicap at Chester (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; may be open to further improvement but that win came off a mark of just 80 and this is a significantly stiffer assignment.

runners_data.name: Naga
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winning handicapper whose hold-up style suits but needs to find several lengths improvement for this level
runners_data.comment: Completed a hat-trick on 1m2f reappearance and top yard won this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick of handicap wins at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) in April and did well in the circumstances when a never-nearer third at Ascot last month; rises steeply in grade here but still has untapped potential.

races.paceDynamic: Azaniya will set a controlled front-running pace with only Sharpen likely to track her early, creating an uncontested lead through the first mile. The moderate early gallop will allow the hold-up brigade including Estrange, Waardah, Crepe Suzette, Coedana, Patagonia Girl and Naga to settle comfortably before launching their challenges in the final three furlongs. With such a strong contingent of proven closers in this small field, the sustainable pace will set up perfectly for horses that can quicken from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver a sharp turn of foot in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Azaniya sets her typical measured pace without pressure from Sharpen
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop allows the quality closers to settle and unleash devastating kicks, with the class performers able to show their superior turn of foot. Estrange and Waardah have the highest class ceiling to exploit this setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Azaniya gets soft fractions early and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: Her recent Saint-Cloud win showed she can quicken off steady pace, and with only one natural closer firing she might get first run on the field. The hold-up horses may leave their runs too late chasing a fitter, sharper leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling slow with multiple horses still travelling strongly at the two-furlong pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where positioning and luck in running becomes crucial, favouring those with the sharpest acceleration. Crepe Suzette's class and Coedana's improving turn of foot could be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sharpen manages to track Azaniya closely and gets first run in the straight
scenarios.body: The George Boughey-trained filly can use her prominent position to steal a march on the hold-up horses who are still making ground. Her Listed-placed form suggests she has the class to capitalize on tactical advantage.

watchPoints.text: Azaniya could steal this if she gets uncontested fractions and the closers fail to fire after long breaks
Estrange's 224-day absence is a major concern despite her proven class and course-and-distance victory last year
Waardah hasn't raced since the same day as stablemate Azaniya's last run, making their relative fitness crucial
Sharpen's ability to pressure Azaniya early could determine whether this becomes a tactical crawl or genuine test
Crepe Suzette's Group 2 form gives her a clear class edge if the race unfolds to suit hold-up performers

races.name: Betway Silver Bowl Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Laureate Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected strong pace, Doyle's booking significant, 36 days ideal preparation time
runners_data.comment: Travelled well when winning at Sandown and he could have more left in the tank
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to firm on debut; gelded before taking a small-field handicap at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in March and he improved again to follow up at Sandown (1m, good) five weeks ago; launched late bids from the back for those 2026 wins, travelled well last time and could have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tactical speed, Marquand excels at tracking pace, strong recent Newmarket form translates well
runners_data.comment: Considerable promise on all three starts; may well be superior to this opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up last October on both 2yo starts (7f, AW/good), on the second occasion in a novice at Newmarket that has worked out very well; reappeared with a ready win at 1-4 in Wetherby novice (1m, good to firm) and there's every chance that this unexposed colt will be better than today's opening mark.

runners_data.name: Archer Royal
runners_data.note: Needs to bounce back from poor effort, hold-up style suits but 63-day break raises fitness questions
runners_data.spotlight: Won debut (7f, AW) and came third in Group 3 at Newmarket (7f, good) last September; however, he was last of seven in another Group 3 there (1m, good to firm) on final 2yo outing and beaten 10l in a conditions stakes at Kempton (1m, AW) on March reappearance; the latter was a hot race but today's first-time headgear for handicap debut needs to prompt a vastly better show.

runners_data.name: Langstone
runners_data.note: Sharp prominent style, recent gelding operation showing positive effect, may need stronger pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Novice wins on last two starts; could be on an advantageous mark for this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after debut and has left sole that 2yo run (6f, soft) well behind him by winning novice events at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) and Kempton (7f, AW) this spring; did well to score with strong finish last time, having been carried left; promising and probably has an advantageous mark for this handicap debut, especially now upped in trip.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner on good going, Osborne's 5lb claim valuable in competitive handicap
runners_data.comment: Solid efforts on both starts this spring; remains lightly raced but needs a step forward
runners_data.spotlight: Reappeared with close second on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good) last month, followed by a respectable fourth of 11 at Ascot (1m, good; favourite); has had only four races but probably needs to resume improvement.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace, best efforts come from off the pace at York over similar distance
runners_data.comment: Needs to prove the form of his autumn C&D effort can be transferred to handicap level
runners_data.spotlight: Won two novice events last summer; easily best of his six efforts since have both been from well off the pace over 7f on good ground at York, including his second in 14-runner race 17 days ago; back up 2lb but has to be worth a go beyond 7f (dam 2m winner) and needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Sponsor
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with tongue-tie, likely to set demanding pace but stamina question at this trip
runners_data.comment: Improved from his debut when fourth at Windsor 11 days ago; each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Tongue tied when showing significant ability on all three starts, on last two occasions taking minor honours in novice events at Windsor (1m, good to firm) and Newbury (7f, good); needs better on this handicap debut but these are early days and his stable has had recent 3yo winners.

runners_data.name: Sir Albert
runners_data.note: Prominent style with class but 91-day break concerning, 7lb claimer Redman brings weight relief
runners_data.comment: Close Listed 5th (7f, AW) on sole run this year; step up to 1m may eke out something extra
runners_data.spotlight: 2-2 in nurseries last July (7f, good/heavy) and close Listed fifth at Lingfield (7f, AW) this February; has top weight in this hot handicap but 7lb claimer is recruited and the step up to nearly 1m may help.

runners_data.name: Suspended Sentence
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who may have needed comeback run, progressive at this distance last season
runners_data.comment: Good form on soft last September; may have needed comeback but not obviously well treated
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive once upped to 1m as 2yo, winning twice (good to firm/soft) before his Listed fourth in France (soft); may have needed last month's comeback run in the race won by Laureate Crown at Sandown (1m, good to firm; 14-1 from 20-1) but he's not obviously well treated.

runners_data.name: Inishbeg
runners_data.note: Front-running style worked against him last time, 5lb claimer helps but may lack tactical pace here
runners_data.comment: Prevailed in Thirsk maiden last time; may well build on that success and progress further
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth attempt when winning a Thirsk maiden (7f, good) in April; made most when below form on handicap debut at York (7f, good) 17 days ago, which can probably be forgiven from widest draw and he was second favourite that day; 5lb claimer is recruited for this hot race on first crack at about 1m.

runners_data.name: Crest Of Fire
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 65-day break, best form came when making running over this distance
runners_data.comment: The form of his sole nursery run reads well and he easily won an AW maiden on his return
runners_data.spotlight: Made the running when beaten a neck on nursery debut at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last September, which was the second leg of a four-timer for the winner; reappeared with an easy 10l win at 2-5 in a maiden at Southwell (1m, AW; made all) in March and looks well treated today, given that his mark is unaltered since that win.

runners_data.name: Lake Como
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits expected pace but hasn't transferred AW form to turf convincingly
runners_data.comment: Broadly progressive on AW; respectable fourth at Newmarket returned to turf; still in form
runners_data.spotlight: Found serious improvement over 7f/1m on AW but, although running respectably, he's not transferred the best of that form to 1m turf handicaps on last two outings (good to firm/good); this stiffer track may suit.

runners_data.name: Special Dividend
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning from 247-day layoff, tongue-tie applied but fitness major concern
runners_data.comment: Worth a second look in view of his good third of 18 in a nursery at York last August
runners_data.spotlight: Won last summer on first two starts (6f, AW) then kept on for third of 18 in nursery at York (7f, good to firm) that worked out nicely; well beaten in Newmarket Group 3 (7f, good) on final 2yo start, which was followed by wind and gelding operations this March; also now has a first-time tongue-tie; needs to resume improvement in a major way.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who found improvement beyond 6f, needs to prove effectiveness on faster ground
runners_data.comment: Won final two 2yo starts and denied clear run on reappearance; 1m can suit; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ffos Las maiden (7.3f, heavy) last September on seventh start, when going beyond 6f for first time, and he followed up in last-gasp fashion in valuable EBF Final at York (7f, good); denied a clear run when mid-division in handicap at Newbury (7f, good; 12-1) on reappearance and the step up to nearly 1m looks a very good move; one to note.

runners_data.name: Delinquent
runners_data.note: Prominent style with progressive profile, recent Hamilton win suggests handicapper hasn't caught up yet
runners_data.spotlight: Won 1m handicaps at Southwell (AW) in April and Hamilton (good; 6lb higher today) 15 days ago; that's two wins from eight starts and he should be a lot more exposed than most of today's rivals, but he was firmly in charge in first-time cheekpieces on that latest outing.

runners_data.name: Synners Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up style in tongue-tie, strong nursery form but hasn't convinced since switching yards
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in slow-ground nurseries last autumn; could build on his respectable comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Won nursery debut for Joseph O'Brien at Naas (1m, yielding to soft) last September and easily followed up at Bellewstown (1m, soft), both in a tongue-tie; having shot up the weights he reappeared with sixth of ten when 66-1 for stable debut at Ascot (7f, good) three weeks ago, which is his highest rating; could build on that (as he needs to) with tongue-tie reapplied this time.

races.paceDynamic: Special Dividend and Sponsor will contest the early lead with both confirmed front-runners ensuring genuine pace from the start. Their duel should create an honest gallop that will stretch the 16-runner field and prevent tactical maneuvering. The strong pace will suit horses that can travel well in behind and find their best stride late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers and prominent runners with a turn of foot over pure speed horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Special Dividend and Sponsor engage in a prolonged speed duel through the first half-mile
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for hold-up horses like Laureate Crown and Archer Royal who can quicken late. Late runners will have plenty of pace to aim at and can exploit tired leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the early leaders manages the pace cleverly while others burn out
scenarios.body: Horses like Princling and Blue Courvoisier tracking the pace can inherit the lead smoothly and prove hard to catch. Their tactical position allows them to respond to any late challenges while conserving energy early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Favours Speed
scenarios.trigger: If the two main pace-setters settle into a more sustainable rhythm after early sparring
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical allowing handy horses with natural speed to dominate from the front. Horses with early pace can dictate terms and kick clear when the pressure comes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits All
scenarios.trigger: If both main leaders go too fast early and tie up dramatically in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The field compresses and any horse with a finishing kick can win regardless of early position. This opens the race up to outsiders who can produce their best effort late.

watchPoints.text: Special Dividend showing any early sharpness despite 247-day absence as this could create perfect pace scenario
Sponsor and Special Dividend engaging in genuine speed duel through first half-mile rather than settling
Laureate Crown's position turning for home as Doyle often gets these hold-up horses perfectly placed
Blue Courvoisier and Princling tracking the early pace without getting caught up in any speed battle
Sir Albert's jumping and early position given the long break and need to prove fitness first time back

races.name: Betway Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with class advantage who should relish the likely steady pace to unleash her proven 7f finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Won 7f AW maiden on final 2yo start; staying-on 3rd in 6f Newmarket handicap latest
runners_data.spotlight: Classy pedigree; ready winner when upped to 7f (AW) on final 2yo start; pleasing comeback at Newmarket (6f) in April, when a keeping-on third of 13, just ahead of a subsequent Listed winner; unfortunate to run up against a big improver at Ascot (7f, good) since but aims lower here; solid.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up performer who has shown she needs patient tactics and should benefit from the anticipated tempo
runners_data.spotlight: Hooded both starts; never raced smoothly from the word go on Salisbury debut (6f) so did well to force a dead-heat on the line; looked more professional when third under a penalty at Thirsk (7f; also good to firm) four weeks ago and this stiffer test at the trip can suit; should improve.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Habitual hold-up horse returning to her preferred 7f trip but faces a quality field after modest recent efforts
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; quiet start to 2026 but dropping in the weights; well held in 3.42 Wednesday
runners_data.spotlight: Had a wonderful 2025, winning seven times at 6f-1m on a range of surfaces; not much to celebrate this year, and this is her first course run, but back on her last winning mark and a revival should come at some stage.

runners_data.name: Fouette
runners_data.note: Back-of-field type who needs a strong pace to be effective but may struggle if the tempo is too sedate
runners_data.comment: Still needs to prove her best AW form can be transferred back to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Back from absence with two 7f AW wins last autumn, then set fire to her mark by running well in Listed events; highly tried on first two starts in 2026 before running quite promisingly at Goodwood (7f, good; first turf handicap) last week, considering she never had a clear run; can fare better.

runners_data.name: Orchid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with stamina concerns beyond 6f who needs to prove this distance suits despite hood applied for first time
runners_data.comment: 2-3 on AW; 0-4 on turf but some respectable runs and remains lightly raced; not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins at 6f on the AW, either side of a winter break as a 2yo and 3yo; seemingly had stamina limitations back over 7f in the autumn and, while she should come on for her recent reappearance at Newmarket, this is a stiff track on which to prove her staying power.

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can avoid traffic issues but faces stronger opposition than her recent AW successes
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming on reappearance but may have needed it and she was 2-3 previously
runners_data.spotlight: Made most for two 6f novice wins on Chelmsford AW as 2yo; respectable rather than dynamic efforts as 3yo, including in a 6f Newmarket handicap last time behind a wide-margin winner who had no pretensions to being way ahead of her mark; needs improvement for step up to 7f.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who should get an easy lead but must prove her stamina holds after failing over 1m last time
runners_data.comment: Improved with each start as a 2yo, winning two AW novices; market useful now handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Raced clear in 7f and 6f events on the AW last autumn but she was slightly hampered and done with from a fair way out on her handicap debut at Haydock (1m, good); should come on for the run, though, and no surprise if she shows to better advantage in a less competitive race.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Forward-going type whose recent Redcar second suggests she's finding form and can race handily throughout
runners_data.comment: Wide-margin winner of a novice last August; suffered in the weights since; hard work again
runners_data.spotlight: Wide-margin winner of a Lingfield novice (about 7f, good) last August but she's been on much the same mark, with little reward, since handicapping and a recent second at Newmarket was a remote one; needs weight off back.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with stamina doubts whose recent turf form suggests she may struggle against this level despite headgear
runners_data.comment: Only seventh at Newcastle on Good Friday; needs to bounce back and others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Two narrow AW wins at 6f and 7f over the winter months; never involved back on turf at Thirsk (7f, good) recently and although this is less competitive her stamina for a tough 7f like this still has to be proved.

races.paceDynamic: Applesandpears will take them along from the front with no obvious challenger for the early lead, creating a measured tempo over 7f. Lady Kodiac and Just A Girl may sit handy in second and third, but with most of the field consisting of hold-up horses including Albaydaa, Distant Shore, Fouette, and Orchid, there's limited early pressure. The sustainable gallop will allow the patient types to get into striking positions turning for home, with the race likely developing into a sprint finish from 2f out. This pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a turn of foot, as they'll get the tempo they need to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Patient Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely steady and Applesandpears isn't pressured
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade get perfect conditions to wind up their finishing kicks from the back, with the moderate early gallop suiting their patient tactics. Quality types like Albaydaa and Distant Shore can use their class to strike late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kodiac and Just A Girl can position themselves perfectly behind the leader
scenarios.body: These prominent runners avoid the traffic that may engulf the back markers, traveling smoothly into the straight before quickening past a tiring Applesandpears. Their forward positioning proves crucial in a messy finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Applesandpears gets a completely uncontested lead and dictates terms
scenarios.body: The modest pace means she has plenty left in the tank when challenged, allowing her to repel late challengers who leave their runs too late. Her proven stamina at 7f becomes a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of pace creates a sprint and traffic problems develop
scenarios.body: The slow tempo results in a cavalry charge where positioning and racing room matter more than pure ability, allowing a lesser light to exploit the chaos. Horses get blocked and the best don't get clear runs.

watchPoints.text: Watch if any horse challenges Applesandpears early as this would completely change the pace dynamic and favour different types
Watch Distant Shore's jumping - she hasn't raced smoothly from the start in both career runs and needs a clean break
Watch for traffic problems in the straight as eight hold-up horses could create a bottleneck behind the likely slow pace
Watch Orchid's settling with the hood applied for the first time as any keenness could compromise her chances further
Watch the sectional splits as a genuinely slow pace will strongly favour the patient finishers over those who need to race prominently

races.name: Betway Bet £10 Get £60 Handicap

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven stamina who can control the tempo from the front without serious early pressure
runners_data.comment: Won at Newmarket three weeks ago and this progressive colt has gone up just 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has proved reliable and progressive in his short career to date; got up near finish when winning at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last month; that looks solid form and he may not have reached his ceiling just yet.

runners_data.name: Factual
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut with room for improvement, ideally suited if pace is steady early
runners_data.spotlight: Finished well when fourth of 12 on handicap debut at Chester (extended 7f, good) three weeks ago; remains open to improvement and this stiffer track should be in his favour; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Prominent style with progressive profile, hood applied successfully last time and proven at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Placed all four starts and she has won her last two; further improvement when coming from the rear to beat seven rivals at Wetherby (7f, good; hooded) five weeks ago; should stay today's extra yardage and there's almost certainly still better still to come.

runners_data.name: Sovereign View
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner returning from 53-day break, better on all-weather than turf based on form
runners_data.comment: Absent since breakthrough win at Newcastle in October but still unexposed as a miler
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily progressive; won Newcastle nursery last autumn and went down narrowly in Southwell handicap on reappearance; both those runs over 1m on AW (ran respectably on only turf outing); may be ready for a step up in distance but should still be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent second at Haydock, experienced campaigner who knows his job
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times for Karl Burke as a 2yo and ran a cracker when second at Haydock (1m, good) three weeks ago; hard to knock but he has had more goes than most of these and he was nudged up 2lb after Haydock.

runners_data.name: Horu Kanu
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing cheekpieces to sharpen focus, 15 days since last run keeps him fresh
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 and can look a difficult ride; rallied into third at Hamilton (1m, good) two weeks ago; needs to be sweetened up by cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 56-day absence, cheekpieces applied to improve his fluency issues
runners_data.spotlight: In frame all three runs this year, although he didn't go with much fluency when fourth of six at Musselburgh (1m; wore cheekpieces) on latest; more required against some unexposed rivals.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with four-timer under his belt, mark has risen sharply but still unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Unbeaten in four races since tackling handicaps, his mark rising from 56 to 84; again had plenty in hand when beating 11 rivals at Windsor (1m, good to firm); impossible to rule out another step forward.

races.paceDynamic: St Anton will lead or sit prominently, with Secret History likely to press early given his prominent style. The lack of confirmed front runners means St Anton can dictate terms without serious pressure through the middle stages. This creates a sustainable gallop that will build gradually, allowing hold-up horses like Factual, Blue To Blue, Wild Thoughts and Horu Kanu to close from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish, as the moderate early pace will leave plenty in reserve for a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If St Anton sets uncontested fractions and the pace is steady to halfway
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows closers to conserve energy and unleash strong finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Multiple hold-up horses converge late with Factual and Wild Thoughts having the class edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners steal march
scenarios.trigger: If St Anton and Secret History inject more pace than expected from the front
scenarios.body: The stronger tempo stretches the field and prevents the hold-up brigade from closing effectively. St Anton's stamina and Secret History's form progression prove decisive in a staying finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy pace suits improver
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes stop-start with positioning issues in the small field
scenarios.body: The tactical affair allows an improving horse with tactical speed to exploit gaps and timing. Blue To Blue's experience and Sovereign View's versatility become key assets.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider benefits from chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite contenders get caught up in traffic or poor positioning
scenarios.body: A horse like Kanishka or Horu Kanu with nothing to lose gets a dream run through the race. The cheekpieces on both help them stay focused when opportunities arise.

watchPoints.text: Wild Thoughts has won four straight but his mark has rocketed from 56 to 84, potentially reaching his ceiling
St Anton unopposed on the lead could steal a march if he quickens the tempo unexpectedly from the front
Secret History drops back in trip from recent 1m+ efforts, needs to prove 1m is still her optimal distance
Sovereign View returning from 53-day layoff with question marks over his turf form compared to all-weather success
Both Horu Kanu and Kanishka wear headgear for the first time, indicating connections feel they need sharpening up

races.name: Betway Good Luck Arsenal Handicap

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs everything to fall right from the back, course winner but 14 days since last run
runners_data.comment: All four wins at 7f; worth another go over 1m but finished last on reappearance here
runners_data.spotlight: Useful effort in defeat at Beverley (about 7f) last May and confirmed that stiff tracks suit when winning here (7f, good to firm; sole course start) in August; improved again when successful at Ayr later and no surprise if he comes on plenty from first two runs in 2026.

runners_data.name: Candonomore
runners_data.note: Strong closer with recent Bath win, proven at this trip but needs pace to aim at from rear
runners_data.comment: Justified favouritism at Bath (1m, firm) final start for S. Williams; sold for 35,000gns.
runners_data.spotlight: A ready winner at Bath (1m, firm) in April and, having run well over 1m2f in the past, he didn't have  a problem with 1m1f when a close third, just behind Ayr Poet, at Ayr since on yard debut; remains on a career-high mark though so a shade more may be needed.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Inconsistent hold-up horse with tendency to fade in finish, 23-day break could help or hinder
runners_data.comment: Talented but went 0-14 for Iain Jardine, including refusing to race; new yard tries a hood
runners_data.spotlight: Modest 2-26 strike-rate and refused to race once in the autumn; however, he's often run well in competitive races, as when third of 19 at York (1m, good) last July and was hampered next time; creditable return for new yard at Redcar (first-time hood, cheekpieces now refitted) this month; involved.

runners_data.name: Freddie Steady Go
runners_data.note: Another back-marker requiring strong pace, recent turf winner but limited winning frequency
runners_data.spotlight: Cosy winner of minor bumper (good) on debut; had wind surgery after a moderate hurdle debut and, following a couple of fair Flat runs, he caught his rivals on the hop when making all over 7f here (soft) recently; has more to prove off his opening mark but should have some potential.

runners_data.name: Moon Beginnings
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades late, this represents a tactical concern in a race lacking early speed
runners_data.comment: Low-mileage 4yo whose sole attempt over 7f resulted in debut win
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced; sole win came over 7f at Chester last September and he's shown only the odd glimmer of promise in handicaps on AW and turf since; falling quickly in the weights but cheekpieces have a big job to do.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but needs more pace than Eupator alone can provide from the front
runners_data.comment: Ran with credit all four starts 2026; needs a career best to win again; stamina to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins in 2025 and he wasn't far away over 1m1f here in September; in reasonable form this year and this trip will suit better than the 1m4f he ran over at York last time out but it will be a good effort if he can win this off his current mark.

runners_data.name: Ayr Poet
runners_data.note: Experienced prominent runner with recent Ayr second, perfectly placed to track the leader
runners_data.comment: Struggled in competitive Sunday Series Handicap at Musselburgh 24 days ago; similar story?
runners_data.spotlight: All 13 wins have come elsewhere but he does have course form and he did so well when going close at Ayr (1m1f, good to firm) last week; however, he's now 6lb higher than his September win which might be a step too far.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner without blinkers this time, major tactical advantage with sole pace angle
runners_data.comment: 0-4 on turf and has a bit to prove with headgear removed back in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Two front-running wins on Wolverhampton AW (about 1m and 1m1f) early in 2026; no impact behind Candonomore back on turf at Bath last time, when regular blinkers were left off, as today; likely other days.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Strong closer on recent AW wins but turf form more questionable, needs fast early gallop
runners_data.spotlight: Has done well over 1m for new connections, finding plenty for two wins on sand at Newcastle in late 2025; given a break after and two turf runs since, at Beverley and when fourth at Ayr ten days ago, suggest he isn't just an AW pony; can go well.

runners_data.name: Elizabeth Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent style but significant class drop suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Has edged down the weights but is 0-10 and others are more compelling; makes reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Finished close up in 7f events on the AW for previous trainer but two handicap runs either side of a break were disappointing and her stamina will be under pressure back on this track.

runners_data.name: Marry The Night
runners_data.note: AW specialist making turf return off 35-day break, hold-up style needs pace to chase
runners_data.spotlight: Three 1m wins on Southwell AW this year; has also won on turf but he's 15lb higher than when last seen on grass in the autumn so needs to show his form on this surface can keep pace with the AW improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Eupator provides the only confirmed front-running leadership in this 11-runner field, likely to dictate terms from the rail without serious early pressure. Moon Beginnings, Ayr Poet and Elizabeth Bay may track prominently but none are aggressive pace-setters, creating a measured tempo through the early stages. The lack of multiple speed horses means Eupator can control fractions and potentially steal a march turning for home on this flat track. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without expending energy in early battles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eupator Controls Gate-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Eupator breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: Sean Levey can dictate comfortable fractions and kick clear turning for home before the hold-up horses can mount their challenges. The lack of pace pressure plays directly into front-running tactics on this flat course.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Beginnings or Ayr Poet can secure the perfect stalking position behind Eupator's lead
scenarios.body: They get first run on the leader in the straight while the hold-up horses are still making ground from too far back. Tom Marquand or Lauren Young can time their move to perfection from an ideal tracking spot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: The superior class and finishing speed of horses like Candonomore and Count Palatine can overcome their back-of-field positions. A sprint finish from the pack negates the front-runner's tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Eupator goes too slowly early and gets swamped by the entire field in the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble where any horse can win regardless of running style. Multiple horses converge simultaneously making for a blanket finish with the winner decided by who handles the interference best.

watchPoints.text: Eupator breaks slowly or gets headed early by an unexpected pace rival, completely changing the race dynamic
Moon Beginnings and Ayr Poet both commit to tracking Eupator closely, creating more pressure than expected
The pace through the first half-mile becomes pedestrian, negating front-running advantages completely
Count Palatine and Candonomore struggle to get clear racing room in the straight from their back positions
Jez Bomb and Priapos find themselves too close to a slow pace and unable to unleash their finishing kicks
